title: How an Automatic Faucet Senses Your Hands

scenes.title: The sensor emits invisible infrared pulses
Hands return light to the receiver
The solenoid valve starts and stops water

vo.text: Put your hands under this automatic faucet, and water starts without a touch.
vo.speak: Put your hands under this automatic faucet, and water starts without a touch.

vo.text: A small infrared sensor near the spout detects that your hands are there.
vo.speak: A small infrared sensor near the spout detects that your hands are there.

vo.text: An infrared LED sends out pulses of light that people cannot see.
vo.speak: An infrared LED sends out pulses of light that people cannot see.

vo.text: With no hands nearby, that light travels away and little returns to the receiver.
vo.speak: With no hands nearby, that light travels away and little returns to the receiver.

vo.text: Your hands reflect some of the infrared light back toward the sensor.
vo.speak: Your hands reflect some of the infrared light back toward the sensor.

vo.text: When the returned signal is strong enough, a controller opens a solenoid valve.
vo.speak: When the returned signal is strong enough, a controller opens a solenoid valve.

vo.text: Remove your hands, the reflection disappears, and the valve closes again.
vo.speak: Remove your hands, the reflection disappears, and the valve closes again.

vo.text: So the faucet turns reflected infrared light into water flow without touch.
vo.speak: So the faucet turns reflected infrared light into water flow without touch.
